newsitem.title: POLAND: Opinion poll suggests tie in Polish elections.
newsitem.headline: Opinion poll suggests tie in Polish elections.

text.p: Poland's ruling ex-communists and the opposition right-leaning Solidarity bloc are running neck-and-neck ahead of general elections due around September, a public opinion poll showed on Sunday.

The poll by the private PBS agency, conducted during a nationwide constitutional referendum, showed the Solidarity Election Action (AWS) would be backed by 22.6 percent if the vote were held now while the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) would get 22.3 percent.

The PBS poll confirmed results of earlier surveys which indicated the elections would pit the SLD, in power with the Peasant Party (PSL) since 1993, against the AWS, a bloc of more than 30 small rightist groups led by the Solidarity trade union.

The poll suggested the PSL would be backed by only 4.6 percent of voters. But analysts said this result would not necessarily reflect the agrarian party's actual showing because turnout at the referendum was small in the countryside, its electoral base.

The centrist opposition Union for Freedom party would be supported by 7.4 percent while the right-radical Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland and the Pensioners' Party would gain 5.2 percent each.
The survey indicated other parties would fail to exceed the five-percent threshold of support needed to enter parliament. More than 23 percent of voters were still undecided, it showed.
The PBS survey was conducted along with the exit polls during Sunday's referendum on the new constitution. PBS surveyed some 30,000 people at 360 representative polling stations nationwide.
The exit polls showed 56.8 percent voted to approve the constitution while 43.2 were against it.
